text: The following question stood in the name of  Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling –  2 To ask the Minister for Trade and Industry regarding the requirement for all homes to have residual current circuit breaker (RCCB) by July 2025 (a) what assistance will the Government provide to home owners who are unable to assess if their circuit breakers satisfy the requirements; and (b) whether a subsidy will be made available for seniors or low-income families to install RCCBs at an affordable cost.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Since July 1985, all new homes are required to have RCCBs installed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For residential premises built before 1985, most would have undergone renovations and have had an RCCB installed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Energy Market Authority (EMA) has separately also notified all private property home owners of this requirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In their communications, both agencies have informed home owners how to assess if their RCCBs are in good working condition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In addition, the helpline numbers for home owners to call for assistance are included in their notification.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For the minority of residents who did not respond to the earlier round of inspections, HDB will arrange for follow-up inspections and RCCB installations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: HDB will also work with grassroots leaders to provide further assistance to elderly residents on this matter when needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We encourage all home owners to ensure that their homes are equipped with an RCCB and that their circuit breakers are in good working condition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Home owners who require further assistance can reach out to EMA or HDB for help.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, how will EMA and HDB ensure that home owners of older residences before 1985 know of this exercise and what should they do?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some of them received the letter but some may not be able to understand, especially some of the seniors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They may not be able to understand what it is all about because it is a bit technical.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second supplementary question is, can the Minister of State elaborate on the cost associated for 3-room and larger HDB flats?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Minister of State's reply alluded to there being subsidies for those in 3-room and smaller flats.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But for 3-room and larger flats, what are the home owners expected to pay as they will not be fully subsidised?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure him and Members that EMA and HDB have launched concerted public education efforts to reach out to the residents staying in 1-room, 2-room, 3-room and bigger flats built before July 1985 to advise them about the RCCB requirement and also how to check if their RCCBs are working, and if they need any support or assistance to facilitate the installation of RCCB by home owners.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I think I have made it quite clear in my answer and I want to assure Members that, after July 1985, all new homes would have had RCCBs installed on their premises, as required by EMA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This means, majority of homes in Singapore fulfil the requirement of having a RCCB.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Since May last year, they have been knocking on doors for these flats built before July 1985, per my sharing in the earlier answer to the Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Just sharing the numbers for the 2-room flats built before July 1985 – there are about 6,000-plus flats.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Out of these, HDB managed to visit more than 4,400 – so about 74%.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that EMA and HDB will be mounting a concerted public education effort, including sending the official letter in four languages – English, Chinese, Malay and Tamil – to these flats to reach out to them.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the letter, the helpline numbers are provided.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If you would allow me, Mr Deputy Speaker, for example, for HDB dwellers, they can call the HDB branch service line at 1800 225 5432 for help.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition, they can also call EMA's contact centre at 6835 8000.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He also asked about the cost for the bigger flats.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The cost of installation of a RCCB in the flat typically is about $500.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to ensure the safety of the pre-1985 homes with this new requirement and we are mindful of the cost of the installation to protect the home owners.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He asked for some numbers – let me quote from the letter.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Those staying in 3-room flats will only need to pay 5% of the cost, which is about $25.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Those staying in 4-room flats will pay 7.5%, which is about $37.50.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Residents of 5-room and executive flats will pay between $50 and $62.50.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Having said that, families who are facing difficult circumstances will receive help from HDB, EMA and from the grassroots leaders.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I hope I have given him the reassurance.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: You mentioned that HDB reached out door-to-door and that they did not manage to meet 26% of the households that they did not manage to meet.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will HDB be open to conducting another round of door-to-door engagements?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I say this because, in Radin Mas, I have quite a number of blocks that were built before 1985 and during my house visits, I still come across residents, especially the elderly, those staying alone, who ask our volunteers what this letter from HDB and EMA entails and what actions are required.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, I do hope that HDB can conduct another round to reach out to those whom they did not manage to meet in the first round.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to reassure him that this is mission critical for HDB and EMA.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to make sure that every home in Singapore has an RCCB because it is a very important electrical safety device.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the number of HDB flats that were built before July 1985 that did not respond to HDB when they went knocking on the doors, HDB will certainly go back, one on one.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will also rope in the grassroots advisors accordingly and provide them the necessary assistance.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If we identify a particular flat does not have RCCB, we will quickly mobilise and make sure the RCCB is installed quickly.
